title: Demo review — every field a finding can carry

findings.summary: Session cache is read before invalidation completes, returning a stale record
findings.body: The refresh path snapshots the cache before invalidation finishes. When two requests for the same user overlap, the second reads the record the first has already replaced.
findings.failure_scenario: Two tabs refresh at once: the second request restores the permissions of a session that was just revoked, and the revocation appears to have silently failed.

findings.summary: Connection is never released on the empty-payload early return
findings.body: The early return skips the finally block, so the connection acquired two lines above leaks on that path.
findings.failure_scenario: Tenants with nothing to publish hit the early return every tick; connections accumulate until the pool is exhausted, roughly six hours in.

findings.summary: Cursor boundary is exclusive where it used to be inclusive, dropping a row per page
findings.body: The comparison moved from >= to >, so the record sitting exactly on the cursor is skipped rather than returned.
findings.failure_scenario: A client paging through 10,000 rows silently receives 9,900 of them. No error, no gap in the ids, just missing records.

findings.summary: Token verification has no clock-skew tolerance
findings.body: Expiry is compared against the local clock with no leeway, so a server running a second or two ahead of the issuer rejects tokens that are still valid.
findings.failure_scenario: One node drifts forward; a fraction of requests fail authentication with no pattern the user can see, and the failures move around as traffic rebalances.

findings.summary: Identical requests each open a connection instead of sharing the pool
findings.body: The memo key includes the request id, so two calls to the same endpoint never coalesce. Latency, not correctness.

findings.summary: New INFO log serialises the whole request body, about 2MB per call
findings.body: At production volume that is gigabytes a day, and it carries customer data into a system with different access rules than the database it came from.
findings.failure_scenario: 50 calls an hour at 2MB each is 2.4GB of log volume a day, including fields the privacy review explicitly scoped out of logging.

findings.proposed_action: Delete the field and its import, then reply on the thread confirming it is gone.
findings.summary: Reviewer: dead feature-flag field left behind after the flag was removed
findings.body: This is what a card built from open pull-request comments looks like — reviewer, PR and a link to the thread, with the reply the agent proposes to send.

findings.summary: Test asserts an ordering the query does not guarantee
findings.body: The new test asserts the first result is the oldest row, but the query has no ORDER BY. It passes today by accident of insertion order and will flake on a different engine.
